products.title: The lab.
products.lead: Every tool starts from a real problem seen on the court. First we watch how the people who coach actually work: how many hours a report costs, where exactly the time goes, what you need in your hands on Monday morning. Then we look in the scientific literature for what holds up against real data, we turn it into a model and into software, and we put it in the hands of working coaches. One rule holds it all together: if it isn't useful on Monday morning, we don't use it.

method.title:
Scientific method applied to sport.
Three steps for every new challenge
method.s1.title: Observe
method.s1.desc: We start from the court: real sessions, real athletes, real constraints. Before writing a line of code we watched in detail how a strength coach works.
method.s2.title: Model
method.s2.desc: We translate scientific literature into models that hold up on real data.
method.s3.title: Validate
method.s3.desc: Every feature is validated by working coaches. Everything is studied carefully before it ends up in the platform.

team.title:
Few people,
highly specialised.
team.p1: We're a group of sport professionals, physicists and designers working at the same table. It isn't a matter of style but of necessity: turning scientific literature into a genuinely useful tool. That requires the person who knows the model, the one who writes the code and the one who designs the interface to talk every day, with no handovers between departments that never meet.
team.p2: None of us comes only from theory, and none only from product. The people on the scientific side have watched real sessions and know the constraints of a season: the space that isn't there, the data nobody has time to collect, the decisions that have to be made anyway. The people building the software learned to read a report before designing one. Around the group are the working coaches testing TrainMind — they are the real added value of the project, and they are the ones who tell us what is actually needed.
footer.tagline: LAB21 is an innovation lab for applied sport science. TrainMind is the first tool coming out of it.
